tweet_summary: A Selena Gomez fan account claims Miley Cyrus and Ariana Grande 'ignored' Selena's Powerpuff Girls-themed Instagram story tribute after the 2026 Golden Globes; the second image shows Selena's story tagging both.
why_note_decision: The 'ignored' claim is celebrity-gossip framing — whether someone reposted/responded to an Instagram story by a deadline is not a stable, checkable fact, and Instagram interactions (likes/views/reshares) are not publicly auditable in a way a note can authoritatively settle. The original note attempts to debunk with 'reports focused on the positive sentiment of the post' without sources, which is opinion-laden. There is no checkable misleading claim to correct; this is the kind of fan-account framing dispute that doesn't warrant a community note.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is a fan-account framing claim about how two celebrities reacted to an Instagram story — not publicly verifiable in any decisive way. A note saying 'reports focused on the positive sentiment' (as the original did) is opinion, not correction. The correct outcome is no note; any note that takes a side in a celebrity-feud framing dispute is a false positive.

fact_check.claim_verdict: unverifiable celebrity gossip — story exists, reactions of tagged users are not publicly auditable
fact_check.notes: The Powerpuff Girls tribute is real and went viral after the Jan 11 2026 Golden Globes. Public coverage does not document whether Miley/Ariana acknowledged it; this is a feud-framing claim, not a checkable fact.
